items.title: Onaje Allan Gumbs interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 12, 2001

ctx.x: me, I just started working. And they wrote the person who was in charge, Sabu signed a form, I had to send away to show what I was making and all that kind of stuff. So about six months later I get reclassified. So I’m relieved of my CO classification, but in other words you’ll never be called. You don’t have to do service anymore and don’t worry about being called. But since I was working up there in Buffalo and getting paid, and going through this whole thing with the music and the culture and everything, I…

emotional response — emotional responses, although in varying degrees, from being very subtle to almost like crazy. But still the emotional responses are pretty much the same, whether it’s adulation or whether it’s a joy or sadness, a tear, jumping up crazy, whatever, a big smile on your face, whatever.
